title: Facial Expression Awareness Training to Understand and Recognize Emotions
official: The FEATURE Study: Facial Expression Awareness Training to Understand and Recognize Emotions
summary: The purpose of this research is to find out if a computer-based treatment program, called FaceSay, is a feasible and effective intervention for survivors of pediatric brain tumors (SPBT). The goal of this intervention is to improve survivors' facial affect recognition, social attention, and social adjustment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Eligible participants are SPBT who:

1. are between the ages 6-13
2. completed some form of tumor-directed treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation therapy)
3. are off tumor-directed therapy
4. demonstrate difficulties on at least one of the following:

   1. Parent- or self-rated Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Peer Relationships Short Form: T-score 1 standard deviation below the mean, which translates to T scores of 40 or below
   2. Social Responsiveness Scale-2 (SRS-2): T-score above 60 on any scale
   3. Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL): T-score below 30 on social competence scale or T-score above 64 on social problems subscale

Exclusion Criteria:

Ineligible participants are individuals who:

1. have a genetic condition affecting neurocognitive or social function, or severe developmental delays (excluding NF1, ASD, and Moya Moya)
2. are non-English speaking (FaceSay is only available in English and some assessments only have been validated in English)

4\) a motor or visual limitation that precludes computer use
